Lowther Park Zoo Annual Pass
See the animals all year for one simple price
We are launching a new program this spring, and we wanted our recent guests to hear about it before anyone else. --[1]--. Until now, the zoo has sold only single-day tickets. Beginning April 1, visitors will be able to choose between two annual passes. The program was created so that families and other
regular
guests can enjoy the zoo as often as they like for a single yearly fee.
What every annual pass includes
Every pass includes unlimited daytime visits for twelve months. --[2]--. Holders also receive ten percent off at the gift shop and café, as well as a seasonal visitor guide mailed to their homes.
Premium extras
The Premium Pass costs a little more but covers much more. It adds two free guest tickets each month, so friends or relatives can join you on your visits. --[3]--. Premium holders may also take part in small-group morning walks led by zoo staff before the gates open to the public.
How to join
The Standard Pass is $55 per person per year, and the Premium Pass is $90. --[4]--. Anyone who chooses the Premium Pass and enrolls by March 20 will also receive a welcome kit with a zoo water bottle.
To sign up, mark your choice of pass on the enclosed enrollment card and return it by mail or at the ticket office. You may also enroll at www.lowtherparkzoo.org.

To: Keith Donnelly
From: Louise Carvalho
Date: October 20
Subject: Team appreciation dinner
Dear Mr. Donnelly,
I have started planning our team's appreciation dinner for November 14. Last year, many people found the restaurant's main dining area too noisy for conversation. Now that we have 52 people on the team, I suggest booking a private room.
I have considered four restaurants near the office: Pellini's, Saffron House, The Brass Kettle, and Blue Heron Grill. I recommend the one reviewed in the October 9 issue of Midtown Guide, as it can seat all of us in one room.
A draft of the evening's program, including your welcome, is attached. Irene Batista, who has been with the company longer than anyone else on our team, has agreed to take part. Please let me know of any changes before I confirm the booking.
Best regards,
Louise Carvalho
Office Coordinator, Customer Service
----------------------
Midtown Guide
October 9 Issue
Blue Heron Grill Welcomes Groups Large and Small
By Paul Nakamura
Blue Heron Grill, on a quiet corner near the river, has a warm, relaxed atmosphere, and a pianist plays in the main dining room most evenings.
The menu is short but well chosen, and the grilled fish was fresh and simply prepared. Prices are also lower than at Harlow's, a similar restaurant two streets away.
The restaurant also suits group events. Its private room, located behind the main dining room, opens onto a small garden terrace. "The room seats up to 60 guests, and we plan the menu with each group in advance," said owner Grace Mwangi.
